question: How would you design and document a comprehensive API for third-party developers? Discuss documentation tools and best practices.

keyPoints: OpenAPI/Swagger specification for machine-readable API definition
Documentation should include: endpoints, request/response schemas, authentication, rate limits, examples
Interactive documentation with try-it-out feature (Swagger UI, Redoc)
Provide SDKs in popular languages to reduce integration friction
Include getting started guide, tutorials, error handling guide, changelog
expectedAnswer.explanation: Comprehensive API documentation requires multiple layers: (1) OpenAPI/Swagger spec provides formal definition of endpoints, schemas, authentication. Auto-generate from code annotations. (2) Interactive documentation (Swagger UI) lets developers test API directly in browser. (3) Getting started guide with authentication setup, first API call, common patterns. (4) Detailed guides for complex flows (pagination, webhooks, batch operations). (5) Code examples in multiple languages. (6) SDKs/client libraries reduce integration effort. (7) Changelog documenting all API changes. Best practices: keep docs synchronized with code, include realistic examples, document rate limits and errors, provide sandbox environment, show curl examples alongside SDKs.

followUps: How do you ensure API documentation stays synchronized with code?
What information should be included in API error responses?
